questions.title: Binomial Coefficient
questions.description:
Pascal's triangle is the canonical tabulation: C(n, k) = C(n-1, k-1) + C(n-1, k), with the borders C(n, 0) = C(n, n) = 1. Build the triangle row by row and read off the entry — no factorials needed.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def binomial(n, k):

Return C(n, k) computed with a Pascal triangle table (row by row).

Input Format:
One line: n k.

Output Format:
One line with C(n, k).

Constraints:
0 <= k <= n <= 30

questions.title: Fibonacci Number
questions.description:
The Fibonacci sequence 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, ... defines each term as the sum of the two before it. The DP way: keep the last two values and roll them forward — no exponential naive recursion. Compute fib(n).

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def fibonacci(n):

Return the n-th Fibonacci number with fib(0) = 0, fib(1) = 1. A rolling pair (or a small table) keeps it linear.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with fib(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Climbing Stairs Ways
questions.description:
A staircase has n steps; each move climbs 1 or 2 steps. The number of distinct ways to reach the top follows the same recurrence as Fibonacci — ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2) with ways(1) = 1, ways(2) = 2. Count them with DP.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def stairs_ways(n):

Return the number of distinct 1/2-step sequences that reach step n. A rolling pair keeps it linear.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of ways.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Tribonacci Number
questions.description:
The Tribonacci sequence 0, 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, ... sums the THREE previous terms: T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2) + T(n-3), with T(0) = 0, T(1) = T(2) = 1. Same DP pattern, one more rolling register.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def tribonacci(n):

Return T(n). A rolling triple (or a list grown to n) keeps it linear.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with T(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 35

questions.title: Stripes Without Neighbours
questions.description:
A strip of n tiles is painted 0/1 per tile, but no two ADJACENT tiles may both be 1. How many valid strips exist? Let f(n) count length-n strips; the last tile is 0 (f(n-1) ways) or 1 (forcing a 0 before it, f(n-2) ways) — the Fibonacci recurrence with f(0) = 1, f(1) = 2. Tabulate it.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def stripe_count(n):

Return the number of length-n 0/1 strings with no two adjacent 1s. A rolling pair over f(n-1), f(n-2) suffices.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of valid strips.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Frog Climb Cost
questions.description:
A frog climbs a flight of steps; step i costs cost[i] to stand on. From the ground it may start on step 0 or 1, and each jump moves up 1 or 2 steps — the goal is to get PAST the last step paying as little as possible. The recurrence best(i) = cost[i] + min(best(i-1), best(i-2)) rolls with just two variables: a memory-optimised DP.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def min_cost(cost):

cost is the list of step costs. Roll two variables through the array and return the minimum total cost to reach the top.

Input Format:
One line: the step costs, space-separated.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum cost.

Constraints:
1 <= len(cost) <= 30
1 <= cost[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Rabbit Colony
questions.description:
A hatchery tracks a rabbit colony: the pair count in month 1 is 1, in month 2 is 1, and each later month the count is the sum of the two previous months (mature pairs breed new ones). Project the colony size for month m — Fibonacci, dressed as demographics.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def rabbit_pairs(months):

Return the pair count in month months (month 1 -> 1, month 2 -> 1, month m -> sum of months m-1 and m-2). Roll a pair of values forward.

Input Format:
One line: months.

Output Format:
One line with the pair count.

Constraints:
1 <= months <= 30

questions.title: Tiling the Balcony
questions.description:
A balcony strip is 2 units tall and n units long; it must be paved with 2x1 domino tiles (laid flat or upright). The number of tilings T(n) satisfies T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2) — the last column is one upright domino or two flat ones. T(1) = 1, T(2) = 2. Count the tilings.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def tiling_ways(n):

Return the number of ways to tile a 2xn strip with dominoes. A rolling pair keeps it linear.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of tilings.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 30

questions.title: Lottery Number Picks
questions.description:
A lottery ticket lets a player pick k numbers out of n; the prize draw order does not matter, so the number of distinct tickets is C(n, k). Tabulate Pascal's triangle and report how many distinct tickets exist.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def binomial(n, k):

Return C(n, k) from a Pascal triangle table built row by row.

Input Format:
One line: n k.

Output Format:
One line with the number of distinct tickets.

Constraints:
0 <= k <= n <= 60

questions.title: Neon Sign Combos
questions.description:
A neon strip has n bulbs, each either on or off, but safety rules forbid two ADJACENT bulbs both on. The production sheet needs the count of legal configurations — the same recurrence as the no-adjacent-1 strings: g(1) = 2, g(2) = 3, g(n) = g(n-1) + g(n-2).

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def sign_combos(n):

Return the number of length-n on/off patterns with no two adjacent ons. Roll the recurrence forward.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of legal configurations.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Vending Machine Refill
questions.description:
A vending machine pays change with ARBITRARY coin denominations (maybe odd ones like 3 or 7 — no greedy guarantee!). The DP way: for every amount a from 1 to target, try each coin and keep the best. Report the fewest coins, or -1 when the amount cannot be paid. No imports — pure Python only.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def min_coins(coins, amount):

coins is the list of available denominations. Tabulate a dp array over 0..amount (dp[0] = 0), relaxing dp[a] = min(dp[a - c] + 1) over usable coins, and return dp[amount] or -1 when unreachable.

Input Format:
Line 1: the coin denominations, space-separated.
Line 2: the amount.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of coins, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= len(coins) <= 10
1 <= coins[i] <= 1000
0 <= amount <= 100

questions.title: Museum Night Patrol
questions.description:
A night guard walks a corridor of exhibit rooms; room i holds cash[i] worth of donations. The patrol policy forbids visiting two ADJACENT rooms (the alarm would trip). The DP: best(i) = max(best(i-1), cash[i] + best(i-2)) — the classic house robber. Maximize the take. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def max_loot(cash):

cash is the list of room values. Tabulate dp over the rooms (dp[0] = cash[0], dp[1] = max of the first two, dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], cash[i] + dp[i-2])) and return dp at the last room.

Input Format:
One line: the room values, space-separated.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum loot.

Constraints:
1 <= len(cash) <= 50
0 <= cash[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Number Shrink Puzzle
questions.description:
A puzzle app starts from n and shrinks it to 1. In one move you may subtract 1, or divide by 2, or divide by 3 — but only when n divides evenly. The memoized recursion with functools.lru_cache solves it instantly where naive branching explodes. This drill FORBIDS loops: import functools and decorate with @lru_cache(maxsize=None), recursing purely.

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def steps_to_one(n):

Start the file with "from functools import lru_cache" and decorate the function with @lru_cache(maxsize=None). Return the minimum number of moves to reach 1 (0 moves when n is already 1): recurse on n - 1 always, and on n // 2 / n // 3 when divisible.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of moves.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 300

questions.title: DNA Marker Overlap
questions.description:
Two DNA marker strings share a longest common SUBSEQUENCE — characters that appear in both strings in the same order (not necessarily contiguous). The tabulation: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 on a match, else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Report the LCS length. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def lcs_length(a, b):

a and b are the two strings. Build the (len(a)+1) x (len(b)+1) dp table and return dp[len(a)][len(b)].

Input Format:
Line 1: the first string.
Line 2: the second string.

Output Format:
One line with the LCS length.

Constraints:
1 <= len(a), len(b) <= 50
strings contain lowercase/uppercase letters and digits
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= len(a), len(b) <= 50; letters and digits only

questions.title: Invoice Matching
questions.description:
An auditor has receipts with amounts and must decide whether some SUBSET of them sums exactly to a disputed invoice. Subset sum is DP: reachable[0] is True, and every receipt x upgrades reachable[t - x] to reachable[t] (scanning t downward so each receipt is used once). Report whether the invoice can be matched. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def subset_sum(nums, target):

nums is the list of receipt amounts and target the invoice value. Tabulate a boolean dp array over 0..target and return dp[target] (target 0 is always matchable).

Input Format:
Line 1: the receipt amounts, space-separated.
Line 2: the target invoice value.

Output Format:
One line, True or False.

Constraints:
1 <= len(nums) <= 15
1 <= nums[i] <= 100
0 <= target <= 200

questions.title: Facade Repainting Bid
questions.description:
A painter bids on repainting a row of houses; each house can use one of three paints with different costs, and neighboring houses must differ in color. Tabulate: for each house, the cost of painting it red/green/blue plus the cheapest alternative of the previous row. Report the minimum total. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and matrix building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def min_paint_cost(costs):

costs is a list of [red, green, blue] cost rows. Roll three state variables through the rows (each house adds its own color cost plus the min of the two OTHER previous colors) and return the cheapest final state.

Input Format:
Line 1: n — the house count.
Next n lines: red green blue costs for that house.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum total cost.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50
1 <= costs[i][j] <= 1000

questions.title: Cargo Knapsack Value
questions.description:
A cargo bay holds capacity W; crates have (weight, value) and each crate is taken WHOLE or not at all (0/1 knapsack). The tabulation sweeps a 1D dp array of best value per remaining capacity, iterating capacities DOWNWARD so each crate is used at most once. Report the maximum value. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def knapsack(weights, values, W):

weights and values pair by index. Keep a dp array over capacities 0..W; for each crate, sweep capacities downward updating dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - weight] + value), and return dp[W].

Input Format:
Line 1: the crate weights, space-separated.
Line 2: the crate values, space-separated.
Line 3: the capacity W.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum value.

Constraints:
1 <= len(weights) <= 50
1 <= weights[i] <= 100
1 <= values[i] <= 1000
1 <= W <= 500

questions.title: Longest Rising Run
questions.description:
A sensor log needs the longest strictly increasing SUBSEQUENCE — values that rise while keeping their order (gaps allowed, skipping values fine). The O(n^2) tabulation: dp[i] is the longest run ending at i, built by scanning earlier smaller values. Report the maximum. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def lis_length(nums):

nums is the value list. Tabulate dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) over j < i with nums[j] < nums[i] (1 when none), and return the largest dp entry.

Input Format:
One line: the values, space-separated.

Output Format:
One line with the LIS length.

Constraints:
1 <= len(nums) <= 50
-1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Delivery Route Count
questions.description:
A courier walks a street grid of R rows and C blocks, starting top-left and moving only RIGHT or DOWN to reach the bottom-right corner. The tabulation: every cell in the first row/column has exactly 1 route; each inner cell sums the routes of the cell above and to the left. Report the number of distinct routes. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def unique_paths(R, C):

Tabulate a dp grid (first row and column all 1, dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1]) and return dp[R-1][C-1].

Input Format:
One line: R C.

Output Format:
One line with the number of routes.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 15

questions.title: Rain Runoff Min Path
questions.description:
A field drains along an R x C elevation grid: water enters at the top-left cell and flows only RIGHT or DOWN, and each cell visited adds its runoff value. The tabulation: the first row/column accumulates prefix sums; each inner cell takes its own value plus the cheaper of the cell above and to the left. Report the minimum total to reach the bottom-right. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and matrix building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def min_path_sum(grid, R, C):

grid is a list of R rows of C non-negative ints. Tabulate dp over the grid (dp[0][0] = grid[0][0], first row/column as running sums, dp[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(dp[r-1][c], dp[r][c-1])) and return dp[R-1][C-1].

Input Format:
Line 1: R C.
Next R lines: C values each (the grid rows).

Output Format:
One line with the minimum path sum.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 15
0 <= grid[r][c] <= 100
